transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-02-10
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~38 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Luis (CSM), Evan (VP Eng, MavenGrid), Priya (Head Platform), Liam (SRE), Nadia (Security)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity bump request, EU node activation timeline, and security onboarding for a private VPC pilot. Customer wants a short pilot (3 months) on Dedicated EU nodes, then roll to private VPC if perf and compliance checks pass.

Topics: capacity sizing, regional failover, KMS + audit logs, SOC2 docs, pricing for burst and reserved capacity, timeline for pilot, benchmark run details.

Timestamps and transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everybody thanks for joining, I see most of you, um quick agenda — renewal cadence, eu node activation timeline, security Qs and next steps.
[00:22] Evan (MavenGrid): yup thanks Jordan, we're looking to bump committed capacity by roughly 2.5x for q2, and we need EU presence for data residency. timeline wise we want the nodes live before end of march.
[00:40] Samira (Redwood SE): got it, and are you thinking Redwood Dedicated or Private? last touch you mentioned dedicated then vpc?
[00:50] Priya (MavenGrid): correct — start dedicated eu nodes for predictability and perf, then transition to V-P-C private if the pilot clearance goes well. security will need KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:10] Nadia (MavenGrid): hi — yes security here, we need SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest keys via our KMS (Thales and AWS KMS supported), and a clear egress/ingress plan. also can you confirm log retention and access controls?
[01:34] Luis (Redwood): we'll share SOC2 report and the compliance pack, and retention is configurable — default 90 days in console, can extend to customer SLAs.
[01:48] Samira (Redwood): on perf, for your workloads (short chat-ish queries + long docs) we recommend the nx- flavor — sorry our notes say redwood-verified gpt-like model variants, with batching set to 20ms window and prefix caching. also quantization profile to 4-bit for cost, but we should validate quality.
[02:10] Liam (MavenGrid): small question — we saw some noise about KV cache and token reuse, how does that behave with our short sessions?
[02:24] Samira (Redwood): K-V cache (transcribed as K-V cash in the auto-text, sorry) helps with repeated contexts across sessions. for short sessions, batching gives minimal latency hit and large cost saving. we'll include an example trace.
[02:45] Evan: mmh, latency vs cost is the tradeoff; our SLO for user facing hits is 175ms p95. can Redwood hit that if we increase batch windows?
[03:02] Samira: yes, with continuous batching tuned to your seq length distribution and dedicated GPU pools in eu-west, p95 should be around 120–160ms depending on model selection. we recommend running a short benchmark (we'll supply the harness).
[03:28] Priya: about pricing — rough numbers now? we need a committed monthly and a burst buffer.
[03:36] Jordan: initial proposal: 2.5x committed capacity for 3 months as a pilot, with 30% burst pool and EU nodes priced at premium ~ +12% over standard region. i'll put specifics in the amended quote.
[03:55] Evan: fine — i want to see cost per 1k tokens and also per-embedding if we bump recommendation tasks.
[04:10] Jordan: included.
[04:18] Nadia: on the private VPC path, how intrusive is the on-prem install? do you support air-gapped?
[04:30] Samira: two options — private control plane with VPC peering or an on-prem package. on-prem is heavier, needs a site-engagement, and typically a 6–8 week lead for air-gapped installs. VPC path is faster, usually 2–3 weeks after security signoff.
[04:58] Liam: do you support our KMS HSM provider? we use Thales Luna and AWS KMS.
[05:08] Luis: we have KMS integrations for AWS KMS and a reference pattern for external HSMs; we'll share the integration guide.
[05:22] Priya: great, also need RBAC mapping for our org and SSO (SAML).
[05:30] Samira: yep SAML is supported, RBAC keys map to roles in console. we'll send a short SSO setup doc.
[05:45] Evan: ok on benchmarks — i want a run that mimics our traffic: 70% short prompts (<32 tokens), 30% 512+ token doc completions. can you run that or we run and you interpret?
[06:02] Samira: we can run it in our infra or provide the harness to run against your staging; preference is we run against dedicated eu nodes for apples-to-apples and share the traces.
[06:18] Jordan: timeline proposal: quote to customer by feb 14, bench run week of feb 17, pilot start march 3, eu nodes live march 24, private vpc window april-may if pilot passes.
[06:36] Priya: that timeline works for us if bench results are solid.
[06:45] Nadia: on log capture — can you redact PII automatically? we need that for compliance.
[06:53] Samira: we have redaction hooks and can apply regex or token-based redaction before logs persist; will include config examples.
[07:10] Evan: what about fallbacks? if eu capacity hits saturation can requests failover to us-east temporarily? we need minimal downtime but also data residency constraints.
[07:28] Luis: we can set routing policies: failover to a non-residency region only for non-sensitive traffic or only after explicit opt-in. we will not arbitrarily redirect sensitive traffic.
[07:46] Priya: ok, we'll need that in the runbook and in the contract SLA language.
[07:56] Jordan: noted.
[08:05] Liam: small nit — do you provide per-token cost breakdown at token level and per-route?
[08:12] Samira: yes, Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdown, and trace-level latency. we'll share screenshots.
[08:26] Evan: competitors — we evaluated Anthropic and Vertex; Anthropic was better latency but more expensive in our tests. what's Redwood's differentiation here?
[08:38] Jordan: production-first ops: consistent latency across hosts, intelligent batching and caching, and clear pricing controls. plus the private path for VPC/on-prem that we demo'd.
[08:54] Priya: cool. any gotchas re: tokenization differences? we saw slight variance across models.
[09:01] Samira: tokenization differences can affect embedding costs; we'll include mapping notes.
[09:12] Evan: ok let's recap next steps.
[09:18] Jordan: recap — Jordan sends quote (2.5x committed for 3 months) by feb 14; Samira shares perf runbook + harness by feb 12; security docs to Nadia by feb 12; schedule bench week of feb 17; pilot start target march 3.
[09:40] Priya: and we will confirm KMS provider list and SAML metadata by feb 13.
[09:48] Naomi (silence) [auto-transcript error: speaker name mismatch] — [crosstalk].
[10:00] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in Slack and i'll paste the quote and links.
